original_question: How large are two-particle–two-hole and two-body-current interference contributions to quasielastic-like neutrino cross sections under the actual kinematics of modern experiments, and how can their importance be established directly from observable quantities rather than from indirect sum-rule arguments?
target_in_paper: “Although the transverse sum rule is indicative, a systematic study of observable quantities at the kinematics encountered in neutrino experiments is required to establish the importance of these mechanisms for the QE-like cross section.” (Sec. III C, p. 15)
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies (1) the focus on two-particle–two-hole (2p2h) excitations and two-body current (MEC) interference contributions; (2) the application to quasielastic-like (QE-like) neutrino cross sections; (3) the emphasis on the need to assess these contributions under the kinematics of modern experiments rather than via sum-rule arguments.
missing_details: Specify the reaction channel and nuclear target (e.g. charged-current νμ+^12C→μ+X)
Define 2p2h excitations and two-body current interference (meson-exchange currents with initial/final state correlations)
Define QE-like cross section as flux-averaged, pionless events and double differential cross sections in muon energy and angle
Identify the experiments and neutrino energy ranges (e.g. MiniBooNE flux ∼0.5–2 GeV, MINERvA up to ∼10 GeV)
Clarify “observable quantities” (measured double differential cross section d^2σ/(dE_μ dcosθ_μ))
State the method of establishing importance (direct comparison of model predictions with and without 2p2h/MEC interference against measured distributions)
refined_question: For charged-current quasielastic-like muon neutrino scattering on ^12C with a few-GeV neutrino flux (such as in MiniBooNE at ⟨E_ν⟩≈0.8 GeV and MINERvA up to ∼10 GeV), what is the quantitative contribution of two-particle–two-hole excitations and their interference with meson-exchange two-body currents to the flux-averaged double differential cross section d^2σ/(dE_μ dcosθ_μ), and how can this contribution be unambiguously determined by direct comparison to the measured muon energy–angle distributions rather than inferred from inclusive sum-rule enhancements?
justification: The paper’s open question (Sec. III C, p. 15) calls for a systematic study of observable, flux-averaged double differential cross sections in actual neutrino experiment kinematics to establish the role of 2p2h and two-body current interference in QE-like scattering, rather than relying on transverse sum-rule results alone.
